subject: Capacity velocity ladder and minimal GPU commitment for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@skylinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — early sizing + ramp constraints

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Skyline wants to evaluate a Dedicated capacity proposal tied to an upcoming pilot. High level: we expect to run a mix of synchronous chat and short-batch document generation for our clinician assist features. Target is ~150 concurrent interactive sessions at peak, with most requests <= 1k tokens.

Key asks from our side:
- Minimum committed capacity we can sign to (Skyline prefers a floor to control cost)
- A phased ramp plan that lets us start small and reach steady state within ~90 days
- Latency SLOs we can reasonably expect at 95/99th
- Proof-of-concept/staging cluster to validate throughput before committing

I've attached our initial mutual action plan (Skyline_MA_Plan_v1.pdf) and a rough traffic sketch. Budget guidance: we want to keep first-quarter (pilot) committed spend modest — ideally a 3–6 month commitment with the option to convert to a longer-term reserved contract.

Can you outline a couple of reservation options (min GPUs, ramp schedule, staging approach) that we can review with procurement next week?

Cheers,
Alan
Alan Wu
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyline Health
alan.wu@skylinehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Wu <alan.wu@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early sizing + ramp constraints

Ben / Neha — looping you in to shape a concise proposal for Skyline. Alan, thanks for the details — below are three pragmatic reservation structures I recommend we propose; each includes a staging/test cluster and clear ramp windows. I'll attach a short break-even sketch and an RCU throughput estimate (RCU_throughput_estimates.xlsx) for Ben to validate.

Option A — Lean start (low commitment)
- Minimum committed: 24 GPU-equivalents (can be A30/RTX-class mix)
- Staging: 8 dedicated prewarm GPUs for canary/testing (isolated VPC)
- Ramp: 24 -> 36 by day 30 -> 48 by day 90 (autoscale burst to +20% during peak)
- SLO target: 95th <= 180–220ms (depends on model variant), 99th ~ <350ms
- Notes: Best for conservative budget; allows validation then conversion to larger pool.

Option B — Balanced runway (recommended for latency-sensitive features)
- Minimum committed: 40 GPU-equivalents (mix of A100 and A30 lanes)
- Staging: 12 A100-equivalent prewarm for end-to-end tests
- Ramp: 40 steady; staged increase to 56 if 7-day throughput exceeds threshold
- SLO target: 95th <= 120–160ms, 99th <= 250ms
- Notes: Better tail latency; lowers risk for clinician-facing flows.

Option C — Throughput-first (large commit)
- Minimum committed: 80 GPU-equivalents (for sustained high throughput)
- Staging: 20 GPUs for load tests and blue/green switching
- Ramp: Immediate activation; gradual scale-down policies for nights/weekends
- SLO target: 95th <= 80–120ms
- Notes: Highest cost but easiest to meet strict SLAs.

Operational levers I'd propose we include in the contract: autoscale burst credits, prewarming lanes, and rolling canary windows (3–7 days) so Skyline can validate model deltas.

Ben: can you confirm the throughput spreadsheet numbers for the 150 concurrent sessions baseline and note which model families we assumed?
Neha: please flag any compliance or SOC2/corp security constraints that would affect a staging cluster (networking, logging retention).

Alan — I'll follow up with a succinct one-page comparison for procurement and a DocuSign-ready offer once Ben confirms numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Alan Wu <alan.wu@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early sizing + ramp constraints

Marissa — quick throughput check attached (RCU_throughput_estimates.xlsx). Assumptions: gpt-4o-ish family (medium context), typical clinician prompt mix, prefix caching enabled. Key takeaways:
- 150 concurrent interactive sessions maps to ~30–36 A100-equivalent throughput for 95th tail under our batching profile.
- 24 A30-equivalents will cover functional validation but will show elevated 99th tail (up to ~420ms) under sustained peak bursts.
- A hybrid lane (A30 for baseline + 12 A100 prewarm) gives a good cost/latency balance for Option B.

I'll flag model variants and provide two costed SKU mixes for your one-pager.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@skylinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early sizing + ramp constraints

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the clear options. A few constraints from procurement and platform:
- Our procurement can sign a 3-month commitment quickly, but will cap committed spend for Q1 below what would buy Option B at full A100 weight. They can agree to a convertible ladder (start with smaller, convert to higher-tier within 30–60 days).
- Security: we will need the staging cluster to be inside our VPC with KMS key ownership (we will hand off a key for staging). Neha will coordinate a short checklist.
- SLA ask: Skyline wants a 95th <= 250ms guarantee for the production lane; 99th target we can be flexible on. If you can demonstrate in staging before we sign, procurement is comfortable with a 3-month trial followed by a 12-month reserved conversion.

Immediate ask: can you send a targetable reservation that starts at a 24-commit floor but provides deterministic conversion steps to 40/56 within 60–90 days, plus pricing for the hybrid lane you mentioned? Also include a DocuSign link and a defined POC plan (what we validate during staging).

Alan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alan Wu <alan.wu@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early sizing + ramp constraints

Alan — thanks, understood. Attached is a concise proposal PDF (Redwood_Reserved_Tiers_v2.pdf) and a DocuSign test offer. Summary of the recommended, contract-ready lane we propose for Skyline:

Proposal — "Velocity Ladder" (recommended)
- Signing commitment: 3 months initial (pilot) with option to convert to 12-month reserved term after validation.
- Starting commit: 24 GPU-equivalents (A30-class) active day 1.
- Staging cluster: 12 dedicated GPUs inside Skyline VPC (customer KMS) for a 7–14 day POC test. Redwood will run a 48-hour load plan and provide tail-latency reports.
- Conversion steps (deterministic):
  * Day 30: option to convert to 36 GPUs
  * Day 60: option to convert to 48 GPUs
  * Day 90: convert to 56 GPUs or expand burst credits to cover peaks
- Hybrid lane detail: baseline A30 pool + 12 A100-equivalent prewarm pool available during peak windows. This reduces 99th tail by ~30–45% with modest incremental cost.
- Pricing notes: we included autoscale burst credits and one-time onboarding credits for the pilot in the DocuSign offer. Exact SKU mixes attached in the PDF.

Next steps:
1) Alan — confirm the POC window you'd like (we suggest starting Week of Dec 6).
2) Neha — we'll need the KMS fingerprint and minimal networking allowlist.
3) Ben — please paste the two SKU cost mixes into the DocuSign pricing appendix.

If all good, I'll send the DocuSign link and schedule a 30-min kickoff for the staging plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_Reserved_Tiers_v2.pdf; RCU_throughput_estimates.xlsx; Skyline_MA_Plan_v1.pdf
